resumeFromRunId links a fresh workflow run to a prior persisted run summary and replays that run's recorded agent calls; it is not Pi session continuation, and it never reuses the child's side effects, only its recorded answer text. A replayed call also does not re-read: replay is keyed on the request, never on the state the child observed, so a replayed stage answers about the tree as it was when it ran

replay is keyed on each agent attempt's ordinal position plus its fully resolved request (prompt, agent, capabilityMode, maxToolCalls, model, modelRole, requireModelRole, timeoutMs, maxTurns, label, phase, workspaceMode, workspaceHandle); a shaped call additionally records its return-contract version, so a record written under the deleted text transport (v1) is reported as return-contract-changed rather than blamed on the script as a key-mismatch, is named as a release boundary in the journal, and runs fresh; each same-session correction is part of one recorded attempt. Replay is a strict prefix: the first key mismatch invalidates that call and every later call, including calls whose own prompt is unchanged. A recorded failure keeps its ordinal and always re-runs, and a call resolving to a non-project workspaceMode or carrying a workspaceHandle is never replayed even on a clean key match. The latch fires on key mismatch only, not on a changed outcome: a call that re-runs at a matching key does not break the prefix, so its successors keep replaying answers recorded in a run where that call had a different outcome; because timeoutMs and maxTurns carry no package default and enter the key only when declared, every record written while the former defaults were in force fails the key comparison and re-runs rather than serving text a child produced under a now-deleted implicit ceiling as though the declared budget had been in force

the replay-safety scan is a filter, not a proof: it reads syntax, so access assembled at runtime (globalThis[k] with a computed k, Reflect.get, a root threaded through a parameter), a value smuggled in through process.env or argv, and anything inside an imported module stay invisible to it. The gate that actually prevents a wrong replay is the per-call request key plus the strict prefix latch, which fails closed on any nondeterminism that reaches a prompt or changes call order or count
